pages.claim: Evidence claims require an observable source anchor.
pages.limitation: An anchor proves location, not the truth of the claim.
pages.literal_text:
A-01
CLAIM: Evidence claims require an observable source anchor.
CONCEPT: source anchoring
REASONING: An anchor permits a reader to recover the supporting passage independently.
LIMITATION: An anchor proves location, not the truth of the claim.
PRINTED PAGE: A-1
pages.reasoning: An anchor permits a reader to recover the supporting passage independently.

pages.claim: A paraphrase must preserve the source qualification.
pages.limitation: Equivalent wording may still be disputed by a domain reviewer.
pages.literal_text:
A-02
CLAIM: A paraphrase must preserve the source qualification.
CONCEPT: qualified paraphrase
REASONING: Removing a qualifier changes the proposition and overstates the evidence.
LIMITATION: Equivalent wording may still be disputed by a domain reviewer.
PRINTED PAGE: A-2
pages.reasoning: Removing a qualifier changes the proposition and overstates the evidence.

pages.claim: Page labels and physical page indices are distinct identifiers.
pages.limitation: Some documents omit printed labels entirely.
pages.literal_text:
A-03
CLAIM: Page labels and physical page indices are distinct identifiers.
CONCEPT: page identity
REASONING: Front matter and custom numbering can separate printed labels from file order.
LIMITATION: Some documents omit printed labels entirely.
PRINTED PAGE: A-3
pages.reasoning: Front matter and custom numbering can separate printed labels from file order.

pages.claim: Reference confidence must fall when extraction is incomplete.
pages.limitation: Lower confidence does not identify which missing sentence matters.
pages.literal_text:
A-04
CLAIM: Reference confidence must fall when extraction is incomplete.
CONCEPT: bounded confidence
REASONING: Incomplete text prevents a complete comparison between the draft and source.
LIMITATION: Lower confidence does not identify which missing sentence matters.
PRINTED PAGE: A-4
pages.reasoning: Incomplete text prevents a complete comparison between the draft and source.

pages.claim: A concept label summarizes the role of a passage.
pages.limitation: A passage can legitimately support more than one concept.
pages.literal_text:
B-01
CLAIM: A concept label summarizes the role of a passage.
CONCEPT: concept identification
REASONING: The label groups the passage by function rather than copying its wording.
LIMITATION: A passage can legitimately support more than one concept.
PRINTED PAGE: 11
pages.reasoning: The label groups the passage by function rather than copying its wording.

pages.claim: Reasoning links evidence to a conclusion through explicit warrants.
pages.limitation: Not every warrant is stated by the source author.
pages.literal_text:
B-02
CLAIM: Reasoning links evidence to a conclusion through explicit warrants.
CONCEPT: argument warrant
REASONING: Making the warrant explicit exposes assumptions that can be reviewed.
LIMITATION: Not every warrant is stated by the source author.
PRINTED PAGE: 12
pages.reasoning: Making the warrant explicit exposes assumptions that can be reviewed.

pages.claim: Quotation and paraphrase require separate provenance records.
pages.limitation: Both modes can still misrepresent surrounding context.
pages.literal_text:
B-03
CLAIM: Quotation and paraphrase require separate provenance records.
CONCEPT: reference mode
REASONING: A quotation preserves exact words while a paraphrase records a semantic transformation.
LIMITATION: Both modes can still misrepresent surrounding context.
PRINTED PAGE: 13
pages.reasoning: A quotation preserves exact words while a paraphrase records a semantic transformation.

pages.claim: Conflicting sources should remain visible in a formal report.
pages.limitation: The presence of disagreement does not decide which source is stronger.
pages.literal_text:
B-04
CLAIM: Conflicting sources should remain visible in a formal report.
CONCEPT: source disagreement
REASONING: Visible disagreement prevents a synthesized conclusion from appearing unanimous.
LIMITATION: The presence of disagreement does not decide which source is stronger.
PRINTED PAGE: 14
pages.reasoning: Visible disagreement prevents a synthesized conclusion from appearing unanimous.

pages.claim: A reference audit must bind findings to the current source bytes.
pages.limitation: A hash cannot establish authorship or publication quality.
pages.literal_text:
B-05
CLAIM: A reference audit must bind findings to the current source bytes.
CONCEPT: hash-bound audit
REASONING: Content hashes reveal whether cited material changed after analysis.
LIMITATION: A hash cannot establish authorship or publication quality.
PRINTED PAGE: 15
pages.reasoning: Content hashes reveal whether cited material changed after analysis.

pages.claim: Raster pages require OCR before text-level reference checks.
pages.limitation: OCR can confuse characters and page layout.
pages.literal_text:
S-01
CLAIM: Raster pages require OCR before text-level reference checks.
CONCEPT: OCR dependency
REASONING: A raster image has pixels but no native character sequence for passage matching.
LIMITATION: OCR can confuse characters and page layout.
PRINTED PAGE: SCAN-1
pages.reasoning: A raster image has pixels but no native character sequence for passage matching.

pages.claim: OCR-derived quotations require lower confidence than native text.
pages.limitation: Manual review may still be required for critical quotations.
pages.literal_text:
S-02
CLAIM: OCR-derived quotations require lower confidence than native text.
CONCEPT: OCR uncertainty
REASONING: Recognition errors can alter exact wording even when the visible page is unchanged.
LIMITATION: Manual review may still be required for critical quotations.
PRINTED PAGE: SCAN-2
pages.reasoning: Recognition errors can alter exact wording even when the visible page is unchanged.
